mainEntity.name: How much bone is needed for narrow-diameter implants?

acceptedAnswer.text: Narrow-diameter implants typically require a minimum bone width of 4-5mm and adequate height of at least 8-10mm, though specific requirements depend on individual bone quality, implant design, and clinical factors. Professional assessment using appropriate imaging determines precise bone dimensions and treatment suitability.

mainEntity.name: Are narrow-diameter implants as successful as regular implants?

acceptedAnswer.text: Clinical studies suggest narrow-diameter implants can achieve good success rates when properly selected and placed, though long-term data continues to be evaluated. Success depends on appropriate case selection, adequate bone volume, proper surgical technique, and careful loading protocols tailored to individual circumstances.

mainEntity.name: What happens if there isn't enough bone for narrow-diameter implants?

acceptedAnswer.text: When insufficient bone volume exists, options may include bone grafting procedures to increase available bone, alternative implant designs, or different tooth replacement approaches such as bridges or dentures. Treatment planning considers individual circumstances and patient preferences to determine the most appropriate solution.

mainEntity.name: How long do narrow-diameter implants last?

acceptedAnswer.text: With proper care and maintenance, narrow-diameter implants may function successfully for many years, though individual outcomes vary based on factors such as oral hygiene, bone quality, loading conditions, and overall health. Regular professional monitoring helps ensure optimal long-term performance.

mainEntity.name: Can narrow-diameter implants be placed immediately after tooth extraction?

acceptedAnswer.text: Immediate placement may be possible in certain cases with adequate bone volume and favourable healing conditions, though delayed placement is often preferred to ensure optimal bone healing and implant stability. Individual assessment determines the most appropriate timing for each specific situation.

mainEntity.name: Do narrow-diameter implants require special care?

acceptedAnswer.text: While basic oral hygiene principles apply to all implants, narrow-diameter implants may require specific cleaning techniques or tools based on the restoration design and spacing. Professional guidance on appropriate maintenance protocols helps ensure optimal long-term outcomes and prevents complications.
